series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 1/2] mm: refactor find_next_best_node to find_next_best_node_in
series_items.patch_summary: This patch refactors the find_next_best_node function to find_next_best_node_in, which takes an explicit candidates nodemask instead of always selecting from N_MEMORY. This change enables building fallback lists with non-N_MEMORY candidates without changing any existing functionality. The refactor is done by modifying three files: mm/internal.h, mm/memory-tiers.c, and mm/page_alloc.c. The patch has been reviewed and acknowledged by multiple kernel developers.

review_comments.author: David (Arm)
review_comments.summary: Reviewer David questioned the need for find_next_best_node_in() to take an explicit candidates nodemask, suggesting it could be sufficient to pass N_MEMORY as a candidate, and asked if other actual node masks are expected
review_comments.raw_body:
Just curious, for your use case, wouldn't it be enough to pass N_MEMORY?

Or do we expect to pass other actual node masks that are not derived from
node_states?


-- 
Cheers,

David

review_comments.author: Gregory Price (author)
review_comments.summary: Author acknowledged David's concern about the hardcoded N_MEMORY mask in find_next_best_node_in() and explained how the private node series will handle different zonelists, including a custom one built on a subset of N_MEMORY.
review_comments.raw_body:
That is the base case today - and in fact that's what's hard-coded
in the current logic.

For the private node series we will pass:

ZONELIST_FALLBACK:  N_MEMORY_GENERAL    /* general purpose nodes */

ZONELIST_PRIVATE:   N_MEMORY            /* All nodes, including private */

ZONELIST_KTEST:     (N_MEMORY_GENERAL ^ N_MEMORY)  /* private only */


the ZONELIST_KTEST is something i'm still working with - but it gives us
fully isolated pgdat structures that allow a KTEST to treat the node
mutations as determinstic and otherwise unreachable by the kernel
(because the kernel outside ktest can't select ZOENLIST_KTEST).


ANYWAY...

I don't expect us to build hundreds of these zonelists - they are
expensive to construct (space-wise), but that's largely because we
haven't needed to optimize it.

But you could imagine having a custom zonelist built on a subset
of N_MEMORY so that you could do like...

for_each_reclaimable_zone(z) {
	/* Reclaim */
}

and hide all this nasty zone business from other components of mm/ that
really don't need all that complexity (at most they want the LRUs).

~Gregory

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 2/2] mm/page_alloc: refactor build_node_zonelist() out of build_zonelists()
series_items.patch_summary: This patch refactors the code that builds zonelists in a node-ordered fashion, extracting it into a new function called build_node_zonelist(). This function takes a nodemask of candidate nodes and builds a zonelist for each selected node directly into the destination zonelist. The fallback order is printed as each node is added. The patch allows building new zonelists from candidate nodemasks instead of just the default N_MEMORY node state list, without introducing any functional changes.

review_comments.author: Vlastimil (SUSE)
review_comments.summary: Gave Reviewed-by

review_comments.author: Zi Yan
review_comments.summary:
Reviewer Zi Yan questioned the necessity for build_node_zonelist() to have a new zlidx parameter, suggesting it could reuse ZONELIST_FALLBACK like its predecessor build_zonelists_in_node_order().

Reviewer Zi Yan questioned the naming convention of build_node_zonelist(), pointing out that if build_thisnode_zonelists() implies ZONELIST_NOFALLBACK, then build_node_zonelist() should imply ZONELIST_FALLBACK.
review_comments.raw_body:
Why does build_node_zonelist() need to have a new zlidx instead of using
ZONELIST_FALLBACK like build_zonelists_in_node_order() did?

---

If build_thisnode_zonelists() means ZONELIST_NOFALLBACK, why
cannot build_node_zonelist() imply ZONELIST_FALLBACK?

review_comments.author: Zi Yan
review_comments.summary: Reviewer Zi Yan suggested renaming build_numa_aware_zonelist() to a more descriptive name, build_numa_aware_zonelist(), as the old comment mentioned 'NUMA-aware ordering of nodes' and the code uses find_next_best_node_in().
review_comments.raw_body:
Is build_numa_aware_zonelist() a better name? Since the old comment said
"NUMA-aware ording of nodes" and the code uses find_next_best_node_in().

review_comments.author: Gregory Price (author)
review_comments.summary:
Author agreed to use the new build_node_zonelist() function in two places instead of building a fallback list over N_MEMORY, confirming that the patch will need further revision.

Author acknowledged a misunderstanding about the GFP flag for zonelist selection, agreed that build_thisnode_zonelists() should be part of build_node_zonelist(), and suggested refactoring to simplify code.
review_comments.raw_body:
The intent is to build new zonelist over a set of candidate nodes, and
it's also just clearer: build ZONELIST_FALLBACK from N_MEMORY.

With this we get:

build_node_zonelists(pgdat, &node_states[N_MEMORY_COMMON], ZONELIST_FALLBACK);
build_node_zonelists(pgdat, &node_states[N_MEMORY], ZONELIST_PRIVATE);
#ifdef PAGEALLOC_KTEST
nodemask_andnot(&private_only, &node_states[N_MEMORY],
		&node_states[N_MEMORY_COMMON]
build_node_zonelists(pgdat, &private_only, ZONELIST_KTEST);
#endif

---

thisnode actually means ZONELIST_X+1 as opposed to ZONELIST_NOFALLBACK.

Since folks are adamant about not allowing another GFP flag for zonelist
selection (beyond GFP_THISNODE), the result of this is that all future
zonelist additions must carry a FALLBACK + NOFALLBACK variant.

The question you actually want to ask is why build_thisnode_zonelists()
even exists - it should be part of build_node_zonelist()

I can probably follow up this series by just folding eveything into

/* build zlidx and zlidx+1 (nofallback) */
build_node_zonelists(pgdat, candidates, zlidx);

And add a BUILD_ON_BUG/ASSERT that forces any CONFIG_NUMA to have
balanced zonelist additions.

But I don't think it's strictly necessary for any of this, and we're
just shuffling code from one place to another.  Probably I can just add
that improvement when we add the next zonelist.  In the meantime - this
makes it easier to add new zonelists as-is (and just makes the code more
readable).

~Gregory

review_comments.author: Gregory Price (author)
review_comments.summary: Author acknowledged that the build_zonelists() function has been refactored to always use numa-aware ordering, and agreed that this is implied by the 'node' in the name of the new function build_node_zonelist().
review_comments.raw_body:
I think that's a vestige of older version having different ordering
options.  Now the zonelists are always numa aware (except for
!CONFIG_NUMA, which... duh). 

Anyway numa-aware is implied by "node" in the name.

But I don't have strong feelings about the name either way.

~Gregory

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch refactors the zonelist constructors and iterators in the Linux kernel to make them more flexible and modular. The existing behavior of picking nodes from N_MEMORY is made explicit, allowing callers to narrow the set of nodes used for fallback lists. A new function find_next_best_node_in() takes a candidate set as an argument, making it easier to build zonelists over specific sets of nodes. Additionally, the per-node construction loop in build_zonelists() is extracted into a separate function build_node_zonelist(), which can be parameterized on the candidate nodemask and destination zonelist index. These changes enable more flexible and efficient management of zonelists, particularly for generating private node zonelists.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH fstests v2] btrfs: test graceful ENOMEM handling in synchronous dirops

version_history.subject: [PATCH fstests] btrfs: test graceful ENOMEM handling in synchronous dirops

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch adds a test case to the fstests suite that exercises the btrfs filesystem's handling of ENOMEM errors in synchronous directory operations. The test uses fault injection knobs to simulate an -ENOMEM error when creating a directory, and verifies that the operation returns ENOMEM to userspace without aborting the filesystem. The test also checks that subsequent operations, including a mount cycle with orphan cleanup and automatic fsck, complete successfully. Additionally, this patch introduces generic helpers for driving the kernel's fail_function interface in the common/inject file.

review_comments.author: Filipe Manana
review_comments.summary: Gave Reviewed-by

review_comments.author: Zorro Lang
review_comments.summary:
Reviewer Zorro Lang noted that the _inject_function_error helper does not handle the case where the function to be injected is already in the process of being injected, and suggested adding a check for this condition.

The reviewer suggested that the test case injection functionality should also be applied to the 'dir' group, implying that the current implementation only covers the 'sync' group.

Reviewer Zorro Lang suggested invoking _uninject_function_error in _cleanup() to prevent a stale error injection from leaking into debugfs if the test is interrupted, ensuring that subsequent tests are not affected.

The reviewer approved the patch and added a Reviewed-by tag, indicating that they have reviewed the code and it looks good to them.
review_comments.raw_body:
Hi Jeff,

Thanks for the patch! It's great to see fail_function error injection being
introduced into fstests for this.

Just a couple of minor review pointers below ...

---

^^^
Perhaps this should be added to the "dir" group as well?

---

I think we should also invoke _uninject_function_error in _cleanup(). E.g.

  _cleanup()
  {
      [ -n "$func" ] && _uninject_function_error $func
      cd /
      rm -rf $tmp.*
  }

This guarantees that if the test is interrupted (e.g. Ctrl+C) while an injection
is active, the stale injection won't leak into debugfs and affect subsequent
tests.

---

_exit 0

Others looks good to me, with above changes, feel free to add:

Reviewed-by: Zorro Lang <zlang@kernel.org>

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH v6 00/19] selftests/mm: improve khugepaged coverage

series_items.subject: [PATCH v6 01/19] selftests/mm: raise the khugepaged test-case cap
series_items.patch_summary: This patch increases the maximum number of test cases allowed in the khugepaged selftest suite from 64 to 256, resolving an issue where adding more test cases would cause the entire suite to abort before running any tests.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v6 02/19] selftests/mm: skip collapse_compound_extreme() where the PMD is too large
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the selftests/mm/khugepaged test to skip a specific case where the PMD (Page Map Directory) size is too large, causing the allocator to fail reliably. The test in question, collapse_compound_extreme(), requires multiple consecutive allocations of a certain size, which becomes unreliable when the PMD size exceeds 32M. By skipping this case, the patch ensures that the test does not fail abruptly and allows other cases to run successfully.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v6 03/19] selftests/mm: scale khugepaged's collapse wait with the PMD size
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adjusts the timeout for khugepaged's collapse wait to be proportional to the size of the PMD (Page Map Directory). The original three-second timeout was deemed too short for large PMDs, leading to false failures in some cases. The new approach scales the timeout by adding one second for every 128M bytes collapsed, ensuring that larger PMDs have a longer wait time. This change is expected to improve test reliability and accuracy.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v6 04/19] selftests/mm: skip khugepaged page cache cases without a PMD folio
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the khugepaged selftest to skip cases where a PMD-sized page cache folio is not supported by the kernel. The problem arises on arm64 architectures with 64K pages, where the PMD order exceeds the maximum page cache order. As a result, the kernel refuses collapse requests for PMD-sized folios and the test fails. To address this issue, the patch introduces a new function `thp_file_supported_orders()` to determine the supported orders for file folios, and skips the shmem and file mem types where the cap is below the PMD order. The patch also adds support for anonymous collapse, which is unaffected by this limitation.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v6 05/19] selftests/mm: make the swap cases' swapout reliable
series_items.patch_summary: This patch improves the reliability of swapout operations in selftests/mm by introducing a retry mechanism to handle cases where MADV_PAGEOUT is best effort and khugepaged may still be working on the range. The patch adds a new function `swapout_range` that retries swapping out a range up to two seconds, holding it out of khugepaged's reach meanwhile. If the pages still won't swap out after retrying, the test skips the operation. This change aims to prevent false negatives in the selftests due to timing issues and kernel bugs.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v6 06/19] selftests/mm: stop khugepaged during the MADV_COLLAPSE cases
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the selftests/mm/khugepaged.c file to ensure that khugepaged is stopped during MADV_COLLAPSE cases. The problem it solves is that khugepaged was interfering with the test cases by collapsing the very range being tested, causing the tests to fail. To fix this, the patch clears per-order controls in addition to global controls, as MADV_COLLAPSE does not consult these settings. This change ensures that the test cases can run reliably and accurately test the behavior of khugepaged.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v6 07/19] selftests/mm: move is_backed_by_folio() into vm_util
series_items.patch_summary: This patch moves a utility function called is_backed_by_folio() from the split_huge_page_test.c file to the vm_util.c file in the selftests/mm directory. The function checks if an address range is backed by a folio of a given order, which is useful for tests that build or collapse large folios. The patch does not introduce any functional changes and makes the utility function available for use in other tests.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v6 08/19] selftests/mm: add folio-order check for address ranges
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a new function called is_range_backed_by_order() to the selftests/mm module. This function checks if a given address range is backed by folios of a specific order, ensuring that each part of the range maps one folio of that order from head to tail. The function is designed to be used in mTHP collapse tests and requires every folio-sized, folio-aligned part of the range to map one folio of the target order. If any part of the range fails this condition, the function returns false.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v6 09/19] selftests/mm: add folio-order detection self-check
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a self-test to verify the accuracy of the vm_util folio-order helpers, which are used by khugepaged mTHP tests to detect collapse results. The test faults in memory with only one order enabled at a time and checks that the helpers report exactly that order. The test is run ahead of the khugepaged test to ensure that any errors are reported as themselves rather than as collapse failures.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v6 10/19] selftests/mm: add khugepaged completion barrier helper
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a helper function called khugepaged_full_pass to the hugepage_settings module in the Linux kernel. The function is used by khugepaged tests to wait for a full pass of page scanning, which is necessary because the current implementation only polls until the scan counter has advanced by two, but this can be too short if the scan sleep time is long. The helper function uses sysfs to store the pages_to_scan value and waits for the daemon to complete one pass before returning.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v6 11/19] selftests/mm: add order-parameterized khugepaged collapse cases
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds four new test cases to the khugepaged selftest suite, specifically designed to check how khugepaged handles different window collapse scenarios when the order parameter is used. The new cases cover various edge cases such as a single populated window collapsing, a partial window collapsing with max_ptes_none enabled, a full window collapsing with max_ptes_none disabled, and mixed sources collapsing to the target order. Each case faults its region before MADV_HUGEPAGE with only the target order enabled, allowing khugepaged to handle the collapse. The test cases are designed to ensure that khugepaged behaves correctly in these scenarios, which were previously not adequately tested.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v6 12/19] selftests/mm: parameterize the mixed-source collapse case by source order
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the mixed-source collapse case in the selftests/mm test suite by introducing a new parameter to specify the source order alongside the target order. The source order is used when collapsing contpte-mapped sources into larger mTHP, and the patch adds checks to ensure that the source order is supported and not below the target order. This change allows for more flexible testing of memory management scenarios.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v6 13/19] selftests/mm: cover a shared-source collapse write race
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a test case to the selftests/mm module to cover a shared-source collapse write race in Linux kernel. The test checks that copy-on-write (CoW) isolation survives when a parent writes to a shared range while its child collapses it. The parent unshares one page every 10ms, starting once the child indicates it is about to collapse. This ensures CoW keeps the two apart: the child sees pre-fork content, and the parent only its own writes. The test prepares for changing how collapse handles fork-shared sources.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v6 14/19] selftests/mm: run every supported collapse order by default
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the khugepaged selftest to run all supported collapse orders by default, rather than only running a single order when specified with the -c option. The test cases for memory-type huge page (mTHP) collapse are now run once per supported anon THP order below the PMD, and the context is pulled into both the no-argument invocation and the "all" case. The patch also updates the usage message to reflect these changes and adds range checking for the -s and -c options.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v6 15/19] selftests/mm: check that one khugepaged pass collapses one window
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a new selftest to check the behavior of khugepaged, specifically that one pass of khugepaged_full_pass() can collapse one window with exactly one collapse attempt attributed to its source pages. The test prepares an aligned window, records its source PFNs from pagemap, runs one khugepaged_full_pass() barrier, and checks if the window came out collapsed as expected. The patch also includes four small helpers in vm_util for reading the trace buffer. The test has been passed on x86-64 4K and arm64 64K architectures.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v6 16/19] selftests/mm: add khugepaged race harness
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a selftest harness to exercise khugepaged under contention by simulating various concurrent operations such as faults, GUP pins, fork, mremap, and MADV_DONTNEED on the same address space. The test runs in different modes, including stepped, free, and madvise, each with its own protocol for collapsing pages. The harness checks that a racing page reads either as its original pattern or as zero, ensuring that no other value is read. This selftest aims to identify potential issues related to khugepaged's behavior under concurrent access.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v6 17/19] selftests/mm: race the collapse of windows with holes
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a test to the selftests/mm suite to race the collapse of windows with holes in memory. The test harness pins max_ptes_none to 0, causing khugepaged to only collapse a window once every PTE is present. A window with holes takes a different route and never gets raced. The test runs both ends of the occupancy scale for every driver mode, one after the other, and checks for corruption. The patch also adds code to handle the case where slots count as holes under racing MADV_DONTNEED conditions.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v6 18/19] selftests/mm: add memory-pressure threads to the khugepaged race harness
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds two new threads to the khugepaged race harness: pageout and compactor. The pageout thread simulates memory pressure by repeatedly advising a region of memory for swap-out, faults it back in, and checks its contents to ensure that the page's pattern is preserved after being written to disk. The compactor thread writes to /proc/sys/vm/compact_memory in a loop, competing with the collapse for pages and causing refcount elevations and migration entries. Each test run now includes 12 combinations of modes and occupancy limits, including both with and without these new threads.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v6 19/19] selftests/mm: zap whole PTE tables in the khugepaged race harness
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the khugepaged race harness to occasionally zap whole PMD-aligned areas of page tables, rather than just individual pages. This is done to simulate a racing condition between the MADV_DONTNEED thread and the collapse walking the same table. The change aims to improve the test's ability to detect potential issues related to page table reclaiming.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series improves the testing of khugepaged, a Linux kernel feature that collapses huge pages to smaller ones. The existing tests were incomplete and had issues such as not being able to detect where a collapse landed or exercising collapse under contention. This patch series addresses these gaps by making the suite run at larger PMD sizes, detecting results per window rather than count, driving khugepaged deterministically, covering collapse at every supported order, and racing against sources that can touch its sources. The patches have been tested on an unmodified kernel and all tests pass.

review_comments.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
review_comments.summary: The author is addressing a concern about the MAX_TEST_CASES limit in khugepaged.c, which causes the test suite to abort when adding more cases due to a table overflow. The author agrees that raising the cap from 64 to 256 will resolve this issue and has made the necessary changes.
review_comments.raw_body:
From: "Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta)" <kas@kernel.org>

TEST() ends the run with "MAX_TEST_CASES is too small" when the table
fills, and the table holds 64.  A full invocation already registers 63, so
the next case added anywhere aborts the whole suite before a single test
runs.

Raise the cap to 256.  The table is a static array of small structs, so the
room costs nothing worth counting.

diff --git a/tools/testing/selftests/mm/khugepaged.c b/tools/testing/selftests/mm/khugepaged.c
index 525108cace54..c44bc18f7536 100644
--- a/tools/testing/selftests/mm/khugepaged.c
+++ b/tools/testing/selftests/mm/khugepaged.c
@@ -1290,7 +1290,7 @@ struct test_case {
 	test_fn fn;
 };
 
-#define MAX_TEST_CASES 64
+#define MAX_TEST_CASES 256
 static struct test_case test_cases[MAX_TEST_CASES];
 static int nr_test_cases;

review_comments.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
review_comments.summary: The author acknowledged that the current implementation of collapse_compound_extreme() fails on a 512M PMD due to unreliable allocation of order-13 pages, and plans to skip this case by adding a check for PMDs larger than 32M.
review_comments.raw_body:
From: "Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta)" <kas@kernel.org>

collapse_compound_extreme() builds a PTE table full of distinct PTE-mapped
compound pages by cycling hpage_pmd_nr fault-time THPs through mremap.  It
therefore needs hpage_pmd_nr PMD-order allocations in a row.  That is fine
at a 2M PMD (4K base pages) or a 32M one (16K).  A 512M PMD -- arm64 with
64K base pages -- makes each of those an order-13 allocation, which the
allocator cannot reliably hand out even once, let alone 8192 times.

The failure is not a quiet one: the case calls ksft_exit_fail_msg(), so the
whole binary stops and every case after it is lost.

Skip the case where the PMD is larger than 32M.  The MADV_COLLAPSE cases
still cover PMD-order collapse on those configurations, and 4K and 16K
PMDs are unaffected.

Assisted-by: LLM
Acked-by: Lorenzo Stoakes (ARM) <ljs@kernel.org>
Reviewed-by: Mike Rapoport (Microsoft) <rppt@kernel.org>
Reviewed-by: Baolin Wang <baolin.wang@linux.alibaba.com>
Tested-by: Muhammad Usama Anjum <usama.anjum@arm.com>
Signed-off-by: Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta) <kas@kernel.org>
---
 tools/testing/selftests/mm/khugepaged.c | 10 ++++++++++
 1 file changed, 10 insertions(+)

diff --git a/tools/testing/selftests/mm/khugepaged.c b/tools/testing/selftests/mm/khugepaged.c
index c44bc18f7536..8a6d708026b7 100644
--- a/tools/testing/selftests/mm/khugepaged.c
+++ b/tools/testing/selftests/mm/khugepaged.c
@@ -940,6 +940,16 @@ static void collapse_compound_extreme(struct collapse_context *c, struct mem_ops
 	void *p;
 	int i;
 
+	/*
+	 * This needs hpage_pmd_nr PMD-order allocations in a row, which the
+	 * allocator will not supply if the PMD is very large.
+	 */
+	if (hpage_pmd_size > (32UL << 20)) {
+		ksft_test_result_skip("%s: PMD too large for fault-time THP construction\n",
+				      __func__);
+		return;
+	}
+
 	p = ops->setup_area(1);
 	ksft_print_msg("Construct PTE page table full of different PTE-mapped compound pages\n");
 	for (i = 0; i < hpage_pmd_nr; i++) {

review_comments.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
review_comments.summary: The author addressed a concern that the wait_for_scan() function's timeout was too short for large huge page sizes on arm64 architecture. They explained that raising the timeout costs nothing to passing cases and would only add time to failing ones, proposing to keep the three-second floor but add one second per 128M collapsed.
review_comments.raw_body:
From: "Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta)" <kas@kernel.org>

wait_for_scan() gives every case the same three seconds, whatever the huge
page costs to build.  collapse_full() asks for four of them: 8M at a 2M
PMD, but 2G at a 512M PMD -- arm64 with 64K base pages.  Three seconds is
thin at that size, and the case has reported a failure for a collapse that
was still going.

The timeout is a ceiling on a poll loop, not a sleep: the loop stops as
soon as ops->check_huge() sees the collapse, or as soon as full_scans has
advanced by two.  Raising it costs a passing case nothing.  Across 80 runs
of collapse_full() on arm64 with 64K pages the wait was half a second in
73 of them, with a tail to two seconds.

Keep three seconds as the floor and add a second per 128M collapsed.  A 2M
PMD is unchanged, so x86-64 is too; a 512M PMD gets 19 seconds.

On arm64 with 64K pages a passing ./khugepaged all:anon takes 49 seconds
under TCG before and after this change.

Assisted-by: LLM
Acked-by: Lorenzo Stoakes (ARM) <ljs@kernel.org>
Reviewed-by: Mike Rapoport (Microsoft) <rppt@kernel.org>
Reviewed-by: Baolin Wang <baolin.wang@linux.alibaba.com>
Tested-by: Muhammad Usama Anjum <usama.anjum@arm.com>
Signed-off-by: Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta) <kas@kernel.org>
---
 tools/testing/selftests/mm/khugepaged.c | 7 +++++--
 1 file changed, 5 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)

diff --git a/tools/testing/selftests/mm/khugepaged.c b/tools/testing/selftests/mm/khugepaged.c
index 8a6d708026b7..189cc4fee18f 100644
--- a/tools/testing/selftests/mm/khugepaged.c
+++ b/tools/testing/selftests/mm/khugepaged.c
@@ -561,8 +561,11 @@ static bool wait_for_scan(const char *msg, char *p, size_t len,
 		int nr_hpages, int collap_order, struct mem_ops *ops)
 {
 	unsigned long hpage_size = page_size << collap_order;
-	int full_scans;
-	int timeout = 6; /* 3 seconds */
+	unsigned long bytes = (unsigned long)nr_hpages * hpage_size;
+	int timeout, full_scans;
+
+	/* Half-second ticks: three seconds floor, plus a second per 128M */
+	timeout = 6 + 2 * (bytes / (128UL << 20));
 
 	/* Sanity check */
 	if (!ops->check_huge(p, len, 0, hpage_size))
--

review_comments.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
review_comments.summary: The author addressed a concern that the kernel refuses to collapse pages when the PMD order is above the maximum page cache order, causing four shmem cases to fail and the test to bail out. The author added a new function thp_file_supported_orders() to read the orders the page cache allows, and modified the khugepaged test to skip these cases if they are not supported.

review_comments.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
review_comments.summary: The author acknowledged that the per-order controls need to be cleared in addition to the global controls, agreed to make this change and provided a patch update.

review_comments.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
review_comments.summary: The author addressed a concern about the reliability of MADV_PAGEOUT and wait_for_scan() in khugepaged tests, explaining that MADV_PAGEOUT is best effort and may not always report accurate counts, while wait_for_scan() leaves pages eligible for collapsing. The author added retry logic to swapout_range() to handle these issues, with a timeout of up to two seconds.

review_comments.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
review_comments.summary: The author addressed a concern about moving the is_backed_by_folio() function to vm_util.c by explaining that it's useful for any test building or collapsing large folios and that split_huge_page_test.c already has the necessary building block. The author promised no functional change.

review_comments.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
review_comments.summary: The author is addressing a concern about the need for an mTHP collapse test to know that a range is backed by folios of the target order, and that they sit where a collapse would put them. The author adds a new function `is_range_backed_by_order()` that checks if every folio-sized, folio-aligned part of the range maps one folio of the target order, head to tail, with the head at the start of the part.
review_comments.raw_body:
From: "Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta)" <kas@kernel.org>

An mTHP collapse test needs to know that a range is backed by folios of the
target order, and that they sit where a collapse would put them.  Nothing
answers both: is_backed_by_folio() classifies the folio behind a single
page, and check_huge_anon() counts the folios of an order in a range
without saying where they start.

Add is_range_backed_by_order().  It requires every folio-sized, folio-
aligned part of the range to map one folio of that order, head to tail,
with the head at the start of the part.

A part backed by two smaller folios fails, and so does a folio mapped off
its natural alignment.  The mTHP cases need both to tell a collapsed range
from the one beside it.

Assisted-by: LLM
Reviewed-by: Mike Rapoport (Microsoft) <rppt@kernel.org>
Tested-by: Muhammad Usama Anjum <usama.anjum@arm.com>
Signed-off-by: Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta) <kas@kernel.org>
---
 tools/testing/selftests/mm/vm_util.c | 47 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 tools/testing/selftests/mm/vm_util.h |  2 ++
 2 files changed, 49 insertions(+)

diff --git a/tools/testing/selftests/mm/vm_util.c b/tools/testing/selftests/mm/vm_util.c
index cc5dfd1e6c94..c8c5cd8ab6c1 100644
--- a/tools/testing/selftests/mm/vm_util.c
+++ b/tools/testing/selftests/mm/vm_util.c
@@ -555,6 +555,53 @@ bool is_backed_by_folio(char *vaddr, int order, int pagemap_fd,
 	ksft_exit_fail_msg("Failed to get folio info\n");
 }
 
+/**
+ * is_range_backed_by_order() - check that a range is backed by @order folios
+ * @start: start of the range, a multiple of the folio size
+ * @len: length of the range in bytes, a multiple of the folio size
+ * @order: the folio order to check for
+ * @pagemap_fd: open /proc/<pid>/pagemap of the range's owner
+ * @kpageflags_fd: open /proc/kpageflags
+ *
+ * Every folio-sized, folio-aligned part of the range must map one folio of
+ * @order, head to tail, with the head at the start of the part.  A part
+ * backed by several smaller folios fails, and so does a folio mapped off
+ * its natural alignment.
+ *
+ * Returns: true if the whole range is backed that way, false otherwise.
+ */
+bool is_range_backed_by_order(char *start, size_t len, int order,
+			      int pagemap_fd, int kpageflags_fd)
+{
+	const unsigned long nr_pages = 1UL << order;
+	const size_t folio_size = nr_pages * psize();
+	char *vaddr;
+
+	if ((uintptr_t)start % folio_size || len % folio_size)
+		return false;
+
+	for (vaddr = start; vaddr < start + len; vaddr += folio_size) {
+		const unsigned long pfn = pagemap_get_pfn(pagemap_fd, vaddr);
+		unsigned long i;
+
+		/* Not present, or a tail page */
+		if (pfn == -1UL || pfn % nr_pages)
+			return false;
+
+		for (i = 1; i < nr_pages; i++) {
+			char *page = vaddr + i * psize();
+
+			if (pagemap_get_pfn(pagemap_fd, page) != pfn + i)
+				return false;
+		}
+
+		if (!is_backed_by_folio(vaddr, order, pagemap_fd, kpageflags_fd))
+			return false;
+	}
+
+	return true;
+}
+
 /* If `ioctls' non-NULL, the allowed ioctls will be returned into the var */
 int uffd_register_with_ioctls(int uffd, void *addr, uint64_t len,
 			      bool miss, bool wp, bool minor, uint64_t *ioctls)
diff --git a/tools/testing/selftests/mm/vm_util.h b/tools/testing/selftests/mm/vm_util.h
index f12979a70135..0172003c16dc 100644
--- a/tools/testing/selftests/mm/vm_util.h
+++ b/tools/testing/selftests/mm/vm_util.h
@@ -101,6 +101,8 @@ int gather_folio_orders(char *vaddr_start, size_t len,
 		int pagemap_fd, int kpageflags_fd, int orders[], int nr_orders);
 bool is_backed_by_folio(char *vaddr, int order, int pagemap_fd,
 			int kpageflags_fd);
+bool is_range_backed_by_order(char *start, size_t len, int order,
+			      int pagemap_fd, int kpageflags_fd);
 
 int uffd_register(int uffd, void *addr, uint64_t len,
 		  bool miss, bool wp, bool minor);
--

review_comments.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
review_comments.summary: The author is addressing a concern that the vm_util folio-order helpers may be incorrect, which would affect all cases built on them. The author proposes to directly check these helpers by faulting memory in with only one order enabled and requiring them to classify the backing as exactly that order. They plan to add a new test to run this check for every anon THP order supported by the kernel.
